ov: The Atlantic cod is a large, brown or green spotted fish of the North Atlantic, one of the most widely eaten fish in the world. It lives in shoals, which move inshore to feed after spawning. A 1996 IUCN assessment lists it as Vulnerable.

why.et: One of the most widely eaten fish.

rg: The North Atlantic: from North Carolina to Greenland in the west, and from the Bay of Biscay to the Arctic Ocean, the Baltic and the North Sea in the east.
df: Fish such as herring, capelin and sand eels, plus squid, mussels, clams, crustaceans and worms. Small cod eat mainly crustaceans.
fx: Females release their eggs in 5–20 batches, a few days apart.
Larger cod act as scouts, leading the shoal’s direction.
